definitions.explanation: Describing someone, especially a child, who is quick-witted and sharp in understanding. Carries a positive, somewhat literary nuance.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}は{利発|りはつ}で、{何|なん}でもすぐに{理解|りかい}する。
examples.english: He is clever and understands everything quickly.

examples.japanese: {利発|りはつ}そうな{目|め}をした{少女|しょうじょ}が{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んでいた。
examples.english: A girl with bright-looking eyes was reading a book.

notes: Often used to describe children or young people who show intelligence beyond their age. Has a literary or somewhat old-fashioned tone compared to more casual alternatives. Common patterns: {利発|りはつ}な{子|こ} (a clever child), {利発|りはつ}そうな (looking clever/bright). Related: {賢|かしこ}い (smart, clever — more general and common), {聡明|そうめい} (wise, intelligent — formal), {頭|あたま}がいい (smart — casual).
